Typical cost: 19–33% a year (CBN averages, Sep 2026). Tunde: ₦1,587–₦2,718 interest; Amaka: ₦28,131–₦48,634
What you need: Account history, steady income or business records, often collateral or a guarantor
Main risk: Hard to get for small or informal borrowers; penalty charges if you fall behind

Typical cost: Varies by employer or bank; often a fee or a deduction from pay
What you need: A salaried job; employer or salary-account bank must offer it
Main risk: Next month's pay is smaller; only for people with formal jobs

Typical cost: 1.5–38% a month advertised. Tunde: ₦2,460–₦38,000 interest; Amaka: ₦50,127+ (reducing), more if flat
What you need: Phone, BVN, bank account; no collateral
Main risk: Very high cost for longer loans; late fees and rollover interest; check the lender is FCCPC-registered

Typical cost: Usually set by members; often lower than commercial lenders
What you need: Membership and regular savings or contributions, often for months first
Main risk: Group can be badly run; money tied up; limited by what members have saved

Typical cost: Usually no interest; some collectors charge a fee
What you need: Join a group and contribute every period
Main risk: You may wait months for your turn; risk of a collector or member disappearing

Typical cost: Rate not published on the MFB sites I checked; quoted per borrower
What you need: Business or group membership, savings record, sometimes a guarantor
Main risk: Costs can be high once fees are added; ask for the full repayment in writing
Strain on relationships if repayment is late; the money may not be there
